sec: Presentation, screening recommendations and first-line tests · p842

items.q: The typical presentation of PHA pairs hypertension with:
opts: Proximal/distal severe muscle weakness and loss of power (fatigue)
items.exp: HTN with proximal/distal severe muscle weakness + loss of power (fatigue) from hypokalaemia. (Book p842)

items.q: Renal potassium loss is confirmed by:
opts: Urine K+/creatinine and a raised urine spot K+
items.exp: Confirmed by 1. urine K+/creatinine and 2. urine spot K+ ↑. (Book p842)

items.q: Match the ABG branch in a hypokalaemic patient — 1) Metabolic acidosis  2) Metabolic alkalosis … A) Leads to the PHA/AME/GRA/Liddle/Cushing work-up  B) Renal tubular acidosis (RTA)
items.exp: Hypokalaemia with metabolic acidosis → RTA; with metabolic alkalosis → the hyperaldosterone spectrum. (Book p842)

items.q: Hypokalaemia + metabolic alkalosis with NORMAL blood pressure points to:
items.exp: Note: hypokalaemia + metabolic alkalosis + normal BP = Gitelman/Bartter syndromes. (Book p842)

items.q: Match cause of hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis with HTN — 1) Acquired  2) Inherited … A) AME (AR), GRA (AD), Liddle (AD)  B) Cushing syndrome and PHA
items.exp: Acquired: Cushing syndrome, PHA; inherited: AME (AR), GRA (AD), Liddle syndrome (AD). (Book p842)

opts: A gain-of-function mutation of the ENaC channel
items.exp: Liddle syndrome (AD) = gain-of-function mutation of the ENaC channel. (Book p842)

items.q: ‘The Endocrine Society recommends screening every newly diagnosed hypertensive for PHA, irrespective of age.’
opts: True, but only with a family history
items.exp: Every newly diagnosed HTN irrespective of age is screened for PHA. (Book p842)

items.q: HTN plus target-organ damage at diagnosis or disproportionate should prompt:
opts: A secondary hypertension work-up unless proven otherwise
items.exp: HTN + TOD should be considered secondary HTN unless proven otherwise (renal or endocrine cause, incl. PHA). (Book p842)

items.q: Which is NOT listed among the target-organ-damage markers?
items.exp: TOD = LVH, fundus changes, microalbuminuria, increased central SYSTOLIC BP. (Book p842)

items.q: The old screening method, now obsolete because drugs interfere, was:
items.exp: ARR is obsolete as drugs interfere with the result. (Book p842)

items.q: Match ARR interference — 1) False positive  2) False negative … A) ACE inhibitors, ARBs, spironolactone, dihydropyridine CCB  B) β-blocker, NSAIDs, clonidine
items.exp: False positives: β-blocker, NSAIDs, clonidine; false negatives: ACEi, ARB, spironolactone, dihydropyridine (CCB). (Book p842)

items.q: While being screened, the patient should be shifted to:
items.exp: Shift to α-blocker, hydralazine, non-dihydropyridine to avoid interference. (Book p842)

items.q: The newer screening test on an early-morning sample is positive when PAC and PRA are respectively:
items.exp: Early morning sample: PAC ≥10 ng/dl and PRA ≤1 ng/ml/hr → proceed to confirmatory test. (Book p842)
